# Introduction

This document includes the preprocessing workflow for Affymetrix exon microarrays (HuEx-1_0-st-v2) of postmortem human brain (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex - Brodmann area 9) samples coming from patients with schizophrenia (SCZ), bipolar disorder (BPD) and major depression disorder (MDD) as well as healthy controls (CTL). The *.CEL* output files of the Affymetrix microarrays as well as the phenotype data file in *.csv* format are conduced as input for the workflow. Following steps will be performed: 

1. Load data and remove replicates and samples with missing pH values
2. Data calibration: background correction, normalization and summarization (to core gene and probeset level)
3. Remove controls and cross-hybridization (cross-hybridization only on probeset level) 
4. Summarize to gene, exon and transcript level using median
5. Annotation and removal of multiple mapped exons/transcripts to genes
6. Remove genes, transcripts and exons lying on chromosome X, Y or M
7. Remove genes, transcripts and exons with duplicated expression values (save info in annotation)
8. Batch correction using ComBat

Below you can find the list of packages that are required by the workflow. 

```{r}
# General Bioconductor packages
library(BiocManager)
library(oligoClasses)

# Annotation and data import packages
library(pd.huex.1.0.st.v2) # for oligo::rma function
library(GenomicFeatures)
library(GenomicRanges)
library(rtracklayer)
library(GenomicAlignments)

# Quality control and pre-processing packages 
library(oligo) # for background correction, normalization and summarization
library(sva) # for Combat and hidden batch correction

# Formatting packages
library(data.table)
library(dplyr) # for data transformation
```


# Import Affymetrix data

Now, we will load the raw data *CEL* files produced by the Affymetrix array scanner software. These files contain the measured probe intensities. We also need to save the phenotype information for each sample. 

First, we generate a list including the *CEL* files and paths from a given directory.

```{r}
celFiles <- list.celfiles("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/2018-07-11_gene_expression/raw_data", full.names = TRUE)
```

Now, we will save the phenotype information into a pData variable. The samples need to be in the same order as the CEL files are read in.

```{r}
pData <- read.table("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/2019-04-09_sample_sheet_KW.txt", sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = T)
```

## Remove replicates

Our dataset includes five replicated samples, which we first need to remove from the *celFiles* and *pData* variable. 

| MHRI-ID |        Filename1 (2009)       |        Filename2 (2014)       |
|:-------:|:-----------------------------:|:-----------------------------:|
|  93.087 | afae2196-30-93.087-150709.CEL |   9.175_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL  |
|  93.046 | afae2196-35-93.046-150709.CEL | MU_9.174_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL |
|  97.214 |  afae2196-4-97.214-150709.CEL | MU_9_114_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL |
|  93.052 | afae2196-43-93.052-150709.CEL | MU_9_176_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL |
|  95.146 |  afae2196-6-95.146-150709.CEL | MU_9_107_(HuEx-1_0-st-v2).CEL |

We will only remove the five older replicated files (from 2009). 

```{r}
replicates <- pData[(duplicated(pData$MHRIID) | duplicated(pData$MHRIID, fromLast = TRUE)) & pData$Batch == "A", "Filename"]
# remove the replicates from phenotype data
pData <- pData[-(which(pData$Filename %in% replicates)), ] 
# remove replicates from cel file list
celFiles <- unlist(lapply(celFiles, function(x) if(!(strsplit(x, "/")[[1]][9] %in% replicates)) x)) 
```

Finally, we can read in the CEL files and check, if they are identical with the order of the filenames in pData.

```{r, results = 'hide'}
rawData <- read.celfiles(celFiles) # affyExpressionFS/ExonFeatureSet
pData <- pData[order(pData$Filename), ]
identical(as.character(pData$Filename), colnames(exprs(rawData)))
```

## Add pData to raw ExpressionSet

Then, we check if the sample names in the expression dataset are identical (and in the same order) with the filenames in pData. If they are identical, we can place the pData information into the ExpressionSet.

```{r}
if(identical(as.character(pData$Filename), colnames(exprs(rawData))) == TRUE){
  pData(rawData) <- pData
}
# change sample names to shorter versions
sampleNames(rawData) <- as.character(pData$ShortName)
dim(rawData)
```

## Save raw data

After every long and time consuming step we will save the generated data into an RData file. This step is necessary, so that we do not need to run all above steps again. 

```{r}
save(rawData, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/1_affymetrix_exon_microarray_raw_data.RData")

# remove unneccessary data
rm(celFiles, replicates, pData)
```


# Background Adjustment, Normalization and Summarization (RMA)

## To transcript/gene level

For the background correction, normalization and summarization oligos Robust Multichip Average (RMA) algorithm is standard practice and runs all three adjustments at once. 

To map the exon arrays to transcript/gene level, we have following three options: 

1. **core**: for all annotated RefSeq genes, 
2. **extended**: including RefSeq genes and genes with mRNA evidence, or 
3. **full**: including RefSeq genes, genes with mRNA evidence and genes with bioinformatic/computational prediction. 

As we want to use "safely" annotated genes we will set target to **core**. The RMA algorithm takes a while to process the huge amount of data provided by the Affymetrix microarrays. So, we will save the corrected data into an RData file for further analyses steps.

```{r}
coreSummaries <- rma(rawData, target = "core") 
dim(coreSummaries)
save(coreSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/2_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries.RData")
```

## To probeset level

For summarization to the exon and/or transcript level it is possible to set target to **probeset** as done here:

```{r}
probesetSummaries <- rma(rawData, target = "probeset") 
dim(probesetSummaries)
save(probesetSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/2_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries.RData")
rm(rawData)
```


# Filtering

Before, we can continue with our analysis, we need to filter the core data for controls and the probeset data for controls and cross-hybridization probes. Therefore, we download the "HuEx-1_0-st-v2 Transcript Cluster Annotations, CSV, Release 36 (95 MB, 7/6/16)" and the "HuEx-1_0-st-v2 Probeset Annotations, CSV Format, Release 36 (58 MB, 7/6/16)" (filename after unzipping: HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na36.hg19.transcript.csv, HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na36.hg19.probeset.csv) under the "Current NetAffx Annotation Files" section on the Affymetrix support website (http://www.affymetrix.com/support/technical/byproduct.affx?product=huexon-st). These files contain all the neccessary information for the Affymetrix HuEx-1_0-st-v2 microarrays. All transcript cluster IDs and probeset IDs, without a sequence start and stop information, are removed from the datasets. 

```{r}
# Load Affymetrix Huex1.0stv2 transcript/gene annotation file (downloaded from the Affymetrix website)
huexGene <- read.csv("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na36.hg19.transcript.csv", comment.char = "#")
# remove ids with no start and stop information
huexGene <- huexGene[huexGene$start != "---",]

# Load Affymetrix Huex1.0stv2 probeset annotation file (downloaded from the Affymetrix website)
huexProbeset <- read.csv("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.na36.hg19.probeset.csv", comment.char = "#")
# remove ids with no start and stop information
huexProbeset <- huexProbeset[huexProbeset$start != "---", ]  
```

## Remove control data

The information about the type of probes is given in the column "category" or "probeset_type" of the HuEx information file. We will remove all transcript cluster IDs (coreSummaries) and probeset IDs (probesetSummaries), which are not indicated with the "main" type.

```{r}
# show all gene categories and probeset types available
table(huexGene$category)
table(huexProbeset$probeset_type)

# get all gene IDs with "main" category and all probeset IDs with "main" probeset type
transcriptIds <- huexGene[huexGene$category == "main", "transcript_cluster_id"]
probesetIds <- huexProbeset[huexProbeset$probeset_type == "main", "probeset_id"]

# remove all transcript and probeset types, which are NOT "main" from the gene and probeset summary dataset
index <- which(rownames(exprs(coreSummaries)) %in% as.character(transcriptIds))
coreSummaries <- coreSummaries[c(index), ]
dim(coreSummaries)
index <- which(rownames(exprs(probesetSummaries)) %in% as.character(probesetIds))
probesetSummaries <- probesetSummaries[c(index), ]
dim(probesetSummaries)
```

## Remove crosshybridization data

Microarray technology has one weakness: the fact that an RNA target sequence can bind to a short DNA probe that is not its exact complement, which is also called cross-hybridization. In the HuEx file, we also have the information in how many cross-hybridizations a probe is involved. All probes with a cross-hybridisation number of 1 and higher will be removed from the datasets. This is only necessary for the probeset data. For the gene dataset where are no cross-hybridization probes available anymore. 

```{r}
# show the number of cross-hybridizations per probe
table(huexProbeset$number_cross_hyb_probes)

# get all probeset IDs with zero/0 cross-hybridizations
probesetIds <- huexProbeset[huexProbeset$number_cross_hyb_probes == 0, "probeset_id"]

# remove all probeset types, which are NOT "main" from the probeset summary dataset
index <- which(rownames(exprs(probesetSummaries)) %in% as.character(probesetIds))
probesetSummaries <- probesetSummaries[c(index), ]
dim(probesetSummaries)
```

## Save data

Then, we save the datasets into RData files and remove unnecessary variables:

```{r}
save(coreSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/3_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries_filtered.RData")

save(probesetSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/3_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered.RData")

# remove unnecessary data
rm(index, transcriptIds, probesetIds)
```


# Gene level 

## Summarization

To summarize the core data to gene level, we need to map the transcript cluster IDs to Ensembl gene IDs. For the mapping to gene IDs we generate a GRanges Object out of the Affymetrix transcript information (chr, start, stop and transcript cluster ID) given in the HuEx file loaded in the **Filtering** section. 

```{r}
transcripts <- GRanges(seqnames = Rle(paste0(huexGene$seqname)), 
                       ranges = IRanges(start = as.numeric(as.character(huexGene$start)), 
                                        end = as.numeric(as.character(huexGene$stop))), 
                       id_internal_huex = huexGene$transcript_cluster_id)
```

For the annotation to gene level, we need the information for all genes. Therefore, we load the Gencode file and filter for gene IDs to build our annotation dataset. This generates the necessary transcript cluster ID to Ensembl gene ID mapping for the annotation in the next section.

```{r}
# Load Gencode gtf file
genes <- import.gff("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/annotation_files/gencode.v19.annotation.gtf", format = "gtf")
genes <- genes[genes$gene_type == "protein_coding"]  # get only protein-coding genes
genes <- genes[genes$type == "gene"]  # get only genes (no exons, cds, transcripts etc.)

# Merge the transcript ids to gencode annotation by using the overlap of sequence ranges and generate the annotation mapping dataset
findOverlaps(transcripts, genes, ignore.strand = T)
annoGenes <- mergeByOverlaps(transcripts, genes)
annoGenes <- annoGenes[, c("transcripts", "id_internal_huex", "gene_id", "gene_name")]
```

To summarize the dataset based on gene IDs, we will first rename the rows of the expression matrix to the Ensemble gene IDs and summarize using these IDs and the median (NOT median polish!!) of their expressions.

```{r}
# get probeset to Entrez gene ID mapping
mapping <- annoGenes[, c("id_internal_huex", "gene_id")]
mapping <- mapping[!duplicated(mapping), ] # remove duplicated rows

# merge core expression matrix with the mapping file (to get gene IDs)
expressions <- merge(exprs(coreSummaries), mapping, by.x = "row.names", by.y = "id_internal_huex")
expressions$Row.names <- NULL # remove Row.names column

# Summarize to gene level using median expression
exprDt <- data.table(expressions)
exprDt <- exprDt[, lapply(.SD, median), by = 'gene_id']
exprsSummarized <- as.matrix(exprDt[, -1])
rownames(exprsSummarized) <- exprDt$gene_id
```

Now, we build a new ExonFeatureSet including the gene summarized expressions. 

```{r}
# generate empty data.frame with rownumbers of exprs_summarized as row names for featureData of the ExpressionSet
df <- matrix(NA, ncol = 1, nrow = length(rownames(exprsSummarized)))[, -1]
rownames(df) <- rownames(exprsSummarized)
data <- AnnotatedDataFrame(as.data.frame(df))

# generate new ExonFeatureSet
geneSummaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                     exprs = exprsSummarized, 
                     phenoData = phenoData(coreSummaries), 
                     featureData = data, 
                     experimentData = experimentData(coreSummaries), 
                     protocolData = protocolData(coreSummaries), 
                     annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
dim(geneSummaries)
```

Save the gene summarized data into an RData file and remove unnecessary data.

```{r}
# save data
save(geneSummaries, annoGenes, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/4_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries_filtered_gene_summaries.RData")

# remove unnecessary data
rm(probesets, genes, mapping, exprDt, exprsSummarized, df, data, expressions, coreSummaries)
```

## Annotation

For the annotation we need the Affymetrix Annotation and GENCODE data generated before. As it is not easy to interpret results mapping to multiple genes, we will remove multiple mappings from the dataset and save the annotated data into an RData file.

```{r}
annoGenes <- as.data.table(annoGenes)

# get min start and max stop position for one transcript
annoGenes <- annoGenes[, list(chr = transcripts.seqnames, 
                              start = min(transcripts.start), 
                              end = max(transcripts.end), 
                              gene_id = gene_id, 
                              gene_name = gene_name), 
                       by = gene_id]

# paste chr, start and stop together
annoGenes <- annoGenes[!duplicated(annoGenes), ]
annoGenes <- annoGenes[, new := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = ":")), .SDcols = -c(1, 4, 5, 6)]
annoGenes <- annoGenes[, c(7, 1:6)]
annoGenes <- annoGenes[, location := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = "-")), .SDcols = -c(2, 3, 4, 6, 7)]
annoGenes <- annoGenes[, c(2, 8, 7)]

# NO multiple ID to symbol mapping => no filtering of multiple mapped genes

# now join the expression dataset with the annotation 
fData(geneSummaries)$gene_id <- rownames(fData(geneSummaries))
fData(geneSummaries) <- left_join(fData(geneSummaries), annoGenes)
rownames(fData(geneSummaries)) <- fData(geneSummaries)$gene_id
length(rownames(fData(geneSummaries)))
dim(geneSummaries)
```

Remove genes which are located on the X, Y or M chromosome as they are hard to interpret. 

```{r}
genesToRemove <- annoGenes[startsWith(annoGenes$location, "chrX") | startsWith(annoGenes$location, "chrY") | startsWith(annoGenes$location, "chrM"), "gene_id"]
idsToExclude <- (featureNames(geneSummaries) %in% genesToRemove$gene_id)
# remove transcripts on chr X, Y and M
geneSummaries <- subset(geneSummaries, !idsToExclude)  
dim(geneSummaries)
```

Remove genes which have exactly the same expression values in all samples (so called multi-mapped samples). This is a necessary step, as we would count genes multiple times (mostly genes with the same exons) leading to high non-significant FDR (multiple testing) correction values in the differential expression analysis later. Instead of completely removing them, we just keep one of the duplicated rows and merge the gene, transcript, exon IDs together (separated by a vertical slash: |). We also do the same for all the annotation information in the feature data (fData) and save everything into a new ExonFeatureSet.

```{r}
# 1. Remove duplicated rows and merge rownames of duplicated rows together
expressions <- aggregate(rownames(exprs(geneSummaries)) ~., exprs(geneSummaries), paste, collapse = '|') 
# change rownames to new merged rownames
rownames(expressions) <- expressions$`rownames(exprs(geneSummaries))`  
expressions$`rownames(exprs(geneSummaries))` <- NULL  # remove rownames column

# 2. Merge the annotation of the merged rownames as well
annoNew <- data.frame()
for (rows in rownames(expressions)) {
  if (grepl("\\|", rows)) {
    ids <- strsplit(rows, "\\|")
    idsAnno <- fData(geneSummaries)[rownames(fData(geneSummaries)) %in% ids[[1]], ]
    idsAnno <- t(data.frame(apply(idsAnno, 2, paste, collapse = "|")))
    rownames(idsAnno) <- rows
    annoNew <- rbind(annoNew, idsAnno)
  } else {
    annoNew <- rbind(annoNew, fData(geneSummaries)[rownames(fData(geneSummaries)) == rows, ])
  }
}

# 3. Generate new ExonFeatureSet
geneSummaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                     exprs = expressions, 
                     phenoData = phenoData(geneSummaries), 
                     featureData = AnnotatedDataFrame(annoNew) , 
                     experimentData = experimentData(geneSummaries), 
                     protocolData = protocolData(geneSummaries), 
                     annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
dim(geneSummaries)
```

We do not have any NA's in the gene IDs and/or gene symbols, so we do not need to exclude them. Therefore, we can just save the annotated dataset into an RData file:

```{r}
save(geneSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/5_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries_filtered_gene_summaries_annotated.RData")
rm(anno.Genes, genesToRemove, idsToExclude)
```


## Batch Correction

For the batch correction of the known batches of the microarrays, we will use ComBat from the Surrogate Variable Analysis (SVA) package. We have five batches (1: 64 samples, 2: 86 samples, 3,: 11 samples 4: 3 samples, A: 40 samples) included in the data. A plot as well as a more detailed description is given in the *02_QC_And_Plots.Rmd* script. 

```{r}
exprsRaw <- as.matrix(exprs(geneSummaries))
batch <- as.factor(pData(geneSummaries)$Batch)
modCombat <- model.matrix(~1, data = pData(geneSummaries))
exprsCombat <- ComBat(dat = exprsRaw, batch = batch, mod = modCombat, par.prior = TRUE, prior.plots = FALSE)
# check if the two matrices are in the same order
identical(rownames(exprs(geneSummaries)), rownames(exprsCombat)) 
exprs(geneSummaries) <- exprsCombat
dim(geneSummaries)
save(geneSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/6_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_core_summaries_filtered_gene_summaries_annotated_batch_corrected.RData")
rm(geneSummaries)
```


# Transcript Level

## Summarization from probesets to transcripts

To summarize the probeset data to transcript/exon level, we need to map the probeset IDs to transcript/exon IDs. For the mapping to Exon IDs we generate a GRanges Object out of the Affymetrix probeset information (chr, start, stop and probeset ID) given in the HuEx file loaded in the **Filtering** section. 

```{r}
# Generate GRanges object for the probeset information (with chr, start, stop and probeset id)
probesets <- GRanges(seqnames = Rle(paste0(huexProbeset$seqname)), 
                     ranges = IRanges(start = as.numeric(as.character(huexProbeset$start)), 
                     end = as.numeric(as.character(huexProbeset$stop))),
                     id_internal_huex = huexProbeset$probeset_id)
```

For the annotation to transcript level, we need the information of all transcripts. Therefore, we load the Gencode file and filter for transcript IDs to build our annotation dataset. This generates the necessary probeset ID to transcript ID mapping for the annotation in the next section. (hint: use transcript ID instead of transcript names, e.g. transcript name DCAF8-001 has two transcript IDs ENST00000368073.3 and ENST00000556710.1 and one of the transcript IDs should map to gene AL139011.2 with transcript name AL139011.2-001 instead of DCAF8 and DCAF8-001 => wrong mapping!!!)

```{r}
# Load Gencode gtf file
genes <- import.gff("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/annotation_files/gencode.v19.annotation.gtf", format = "gtf")
# get only protein-coding genes
genes <- genes[genes$gene_type == "protein_coding"]  
# get only transcripts from the genes
genes <- genes[genes$type == "transcript"]  

# Merge the probeset ids to gencode annotation by using the overlap of sequence ranges and generate the annotation mapping dataset
findOverlaps(probesets, genes, ignore.strand = T)
annoTranscripts <- mergeByOverlaps(probesets, genes)
annoTranscripts <- annoTranscripts[, c("probesets", "id_internal_huex", "gene_id", "transcript_id", "exon_id", "gene_name")]
```

To summarize the dataset based on transcript IDs, we will first rename the rows of the expression matrix to the Ensemble Transcript IDs and summarize using these IDs and the median (NOT median polish!!) of their expressions.

```{r}
# remove probesets that do not have a transcript id mapping
probesetSummaries <- probesetSummaries[featureNames(probesetSummaries) %in% as.character(annoTranscripts$id_internal_huex), ]

# get probeset to Entrez Transcript ID mapping
mapping <- annoTranscripts[, c("id_internal_huex", "transcript_id")]
mapping <- mapping[!duplicated(mapping), ] # remove duplicated rows

# merge probeset expression matrix with the mapping file (to get transcript IDs)
expressions <- merge(exprs(probesetSummaries), mapping, by.x = "row.names", by.y = "id_internal_huex", all.x = T)
expressions$Row.names <- NULL # remove Row.names column

# Summarize to transcript level using median expression
exprDt <- data.table(expressions)
exprDt <- exprDt[, lapply(.SD, median), by = 'transcript_id']
exprsSummarized <- as.matrix(exprDt[, -1])
rownames(exprsSummarized) <- exprDt$transcript_id
```

Now, we build a new ExonFeatureSet including the transcript summarized expressions. 

```{r}
# generate empty data.frame with rownumbers of exprs_summarized as row names for featureData of the ExpressionSet
df <- matrix(NA, ncol = 1, nrow = length(rownames(exprsSummarized)))[, -1]
row.names(df) <- row.names(exprsSummarized)
data <- AnnotatedDataFrame(as.data.frame(df))

# generate new ExonFeatureSet
transcriptSummaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                           exprs = exprsSummarized, 
                           phenoData = phenoData(probesetSummaries), 
                           featureData = data, 
                           experimentData = experimentData(probesetSummaries), 
                           protocolData = protocolData(probesetSummaries), 
                           annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
dim(transcriptSummaries)
```

Save the transcript summarized data into an RData file and remove unnecessary data.

```{r}
# save data
save(transcriptSummaries, annoTranscripts, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/4_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_transcript_summaries.RData")

# remove unnecessary data
rm(genes, mapping, exprDt, exprsSummarized, df, data, expressions, probesetSummaries)
```

## Annotation

We need the Affymetrix Annotation and GENCODE data generated before, but first we check if any probeset ID has no gene ID mapping (all probesets have a Gene ID given! => no filtering done here!).

```{r}
nrow(annoTranscripts)
annoTranscripts <- annoTranscripts[!is.na(annoTranscripts$gene_id), ]
nrow(annoTranscripts)
```

Some parts of the data can be mapped to several gene names. As it is not easy to interpret results mapping to multiple genes, we will remove multiple mappings from the dataset and save the annotated data into an RData file (code and text from: https://f1000research.com/articles/5-1384/v2).

```{r}
annoTranscripts <- as.data.table(annoTranscripts)

# get min start and max stop position for one transcript
annoTranscripts <- annoTranscripts[, list(chr = probesets.seqnames, start = min(probesets.start), end = max(probesets.end), gene_id = gene_id, gene_name = gene_name), by = transcript_id]

# paste chr, start and stop together
annoTranscripts <- annoTranscripts[!duplicated(annoTranscripts), ]
annoTranscripts <- annoTranscripts[ , new := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = ":")), .SDcols = -c(1, 4, 5, 6)]
annoTranscripts <- annoTranscripts[ , c(7, 1:6)]
annoTranscripts <- annoTranscripts[ , location := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = "-")), .SDcols = -c(2, 3, 4, 6, 7)]
annoTranscripts <- annoTranscripts[ , c(2, 8, 6, 7)]

# now remove transcripts with multiple gene id mappings
annoSummarized <- annoTranscripts[, .(count = uniqueN(gene_id)), by = transcript_id]  # group by transcript and count number of different Ensemble gene ids
annoFiltered <- as.list(annoSummarized[annoSummarized$count > 1, "transcript_id"])  # get transcript ids with multiple Ensemble gene ids
idsToExclude <- (featureNames(transcriptSummaries) %in% annoFiltered$transcript_id)
transcriptSummaries <- subset(transcriptSummaries, !idsToExclude)  # remove multi-mapped transcripts
fData(transcriptSummaries)$transcript_id <- rownames(fData(transcriptSummaries))
fData(transcriptSummaries) <- left_join(fData(transcriptSummaries), annoTranscripts)
rownames(fData(transcriptSummaries)) <- fData(transcriptSummaries)$transcript_id
length(rownames(fData(transcriptSummaries)))
dim(transcriptSummaries)
```

Remove transcripts which are located on the X, Y or M chromosome as they are hard to interpret. 

```{r}
transcriptsToRemove <- annoTranscripts[startsWith(annoTranscripts$location, "chrX") | startsWith(annoTranscripts$location, "chrY") | startsWith(annoTranscripts$location, "chrM"), "transcript_id"]
idsToExclude <- (featureNames(transcriptSummaries) %in% transcriptsToRemove$transcript_id)
transcriptSummaries <- subset(transcriptSummaries, !idsToExclude)  # remove transcripts on chr X, Y and M
dim(transcriptSummaries)
```

Remove transcripts which have exactly the same expression values in all samples (so called multi-mapped samples). This is a necessary step, as we would count transcripts multiple times (mostly transcripts of the same gene) leading to high non-significant FDR (multiple testing) correction values in the differential expression analysis later. Instead of completely removing them, we just keep one of the duplicated rows and merge the gene, transcript, exon IDs together (separated by a vertical slash: |). We also do the same for all the annotation information in the feature data (fData) and save everything into a new ExonFeatureSet.

```{r}
# 1. Remove duplicated rows and merge rownames of duplicated rows together
expressions <- aggregate(rownames(exprs(transcriptSummaries)) ~., exprs(transcriptSummaries), paste, collapse = '|') 
rownames(expressions) <- expressions$`rownames(exprs(transcriptSummaries))`  # change rownames to new merged rownames
expressions$`rownames(exprs(transcriptSummaries))` <- NULL  # remove rownames column

# 2. Merge the annotation of the merged rownames as well
annoNew <- data.frame()
for (rows in rownames(expressions)) {
  if (grepl("\\|", rows)) {
    ids <- strsplit(rows, "\\|")
    idsAnno <- fData(transcriptSummaries)[rownames(fData(transcriptSummaries)) %in% ids[[1]], ]
    idsAnno <- t(data.frame(apply(idsAnno, 2, paste, collapse = "|")))
    rownames(idsAnno) <- rows
    annoNew <- rbind(annoNew, idsAnno)
  } else {
    annoNew <- rbind(annoNew, fData(transcriptSummaries)[rownames(fData(transcriptSummaries)) == rows, ])
  }
}

# 3. Generate new ExonFeatureSet
transcriptSummaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                           exprs = expressions, 
                           phenoData = phenoData(transcriptSummaries), 
                           featureData = AnnotatedDataFrame(annoNew) , 
                           experimentData = experimentData(transcriptSummaries), 
                           protocolData = protocolData(transcriptSummaries), 
                           annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
dim(transcriptSummaries)
```

We do not have any NA's in the gene IDs and/or gene symbols, so we do not need to exclude them. Therefore, we can just save the annotated dataset into an RData file:

```{r}
save(transcriptSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/5_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_transcript_summaries_annotated.RData")
rm(annoFiltered, annoSummarized, annoTranscripts, transcriptsToRemove, idsToExclude)
```

## Batch correction

For the batch correction of the known batches of the microarrays, we will use ComBat from the Surrogate Variable Analysis (SVA) package. We have five batches (1: 64 samples, 2: 86 samples, 3,: 11 samples 4: 3 samples, A: 40 samples) included in the data. A plot as well as a more detailed description is given in the *02_QC_And_Plots.Rmd* script. 

```{r}
exprsRaw <- as.matrix(oligo::exprs(transcriptSummaries))
batch <- as.factor(pData(transcriptSummaries)$Batch)
modCombat <- model.matrix(~1, data = pData(transcriptSummaries))
exprsCombat <- ComBat(dat = exprsRaw, batch = batch, mod = modCombat, par.prior = TRUE, prior.plots = FALSE)
identical(rownames(exprs(transcriptSummaries)), rownames(exprsCombat)) # check if the two matrices are in the same order
exprs(transcriptSummaries) <- exprsCombat
dim(transcriptSummaries)
save(transcriptSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/6_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_transcript_summaries_annotated_batch_corrected.RData")
rm(transcriptSummaries)
```


# Exon Level

## Summarization of probeset data to exon level

To summarize the probeset data to exon level, we need to map the probeset IDs to transcript/exon IDs. For the mapping to Exon IDs we generate a GRanges Object out of the Affymetrix probeset information (chr, start, stop and probeset ID) given in the HuEx file loaded in the **Filtering** section. 

```{r}
# Generate GRanges object for the probeset information (with chr, start, stop and probeset id)
probesets <- GRanges(seqnames = Rle(paste0(huexProbeset$seqname)), 
                     ranges = IRanges(start = as.numeric(as.character(huexProbeset$start)), 
                     end = as.numeric(as.character(huexProbeset$stop))),
                     id_internal_huex = huexProbeset$probeset_id)
```

Then, we load the GENCODE gtf file and merge the Affymetrix huexProbeset information with it. This generates the necessary probeset ID to exon ID mapping as well as the mapping dataset for the annotation in the next section.

```{r}
# Load Gencode gtf file
genes <- import.gff("/storage/groups/ccm01/datasets/2018_MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/annotation_files/gencode.v19.annotation.gtf", format = "gtf")
genes <- genes[genes$gene_type == "protein_coding"]  # get only protein-coding genes
genes <- genes[genes$type == "exon"]  # get only exons from the genes

# Merge the probeset ids to gencode annotation by using the overlap of sequence ranges and generate the annotation mapping dataset
findOverlaps(probesets, genes, ignore.strand = T)
annoExons <- mergeByOverlaps(probesets, genes)
annoExons <- annoExons[, c("probesets", "id_internal_huex", "gene_id", "transcript_id", "gene_name", "exon_id", "exon_number")]
```

To summarize the dataset based on exon IDs, we will first rename the rows of the expression matrix to the Ensemble Exon IDs and summarize using these IDs and the median (NOT median polish!!) of their expressions.

```{r}
# Load the probeset data (after filtering, but before transcript summarization step)
load("/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/3_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered.RData") 

# remove probesets that do not have an exon id mapping
probesetSummaries <- probesetSummaries[featureNames(probesetSummaries) %in% as.character(annoExons$id_internal_huex), ]

# get probeset to Entrez Exon ID mapping
mapping <- annoExons[, c("id_internal_huex", "exon_id")]
mapping <- mapping[!duplicated(mapping), ] # remove duplicated rows

# merge probeset expression matrix with the mapping file (to get exon IDs)
expressions <- merge(exprs(probesetSummaries), mapping, by.x = "row.names", by.y = "id_internal_huex")
expressions$Row.names <- NULL # remove Row.names column

# Summarize to exon level using median expression
exprDt <- data.table(expressions)
exprDt <- exprDt[, lapply(.SD, median), by = 'exon_id']
exprsSummarized <- as.matrix(exprDt[, -1])
rownames(exprsSummarized) <- exprDt$exon_id
```

Now, we build a new ExonFeatureSet including the exon summarized expressions. 

```{r}
# generate empty data.frame with rownumbers of expr.matrix as row names for featureData of the ExpressionSet
df <- matrix(NA, ncol = 1, nrow = length(rownames(exprsSummarized)))[, -1]
row.names(df) <- row.names(exprsSummarized)
data <- AnnotatedDataFrame(as.data.frame(df))

# generate new ExonFeatureSet
exonSummaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", exprs = exprsSummarized, phenoData = phenoData(probesetSummaries), featureData = data, experimentData = experimentData(probesetSummaries), protocolData = protocolData(probesetSummaries), annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
dim(exonSummaries)
```

We save the data again into an RData file.

```{r}
# save data
save(exonSummaries, annoExons, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/4_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_exon_summaries.RData")

# remove unnecessary data
rm(huexProbeset, genes, mapping, exprDt, exprsSummarized, df, data, expressions)
```

## Annotation

For the annotation we use the anno dataset generated by the Affymetrix Annotation and GENCODE data in the section before. We first check, if any probeset ID has no Gene ID mapping (all probesets have a Gene ID given! => no filtering done here!).

```{r}
nrow(annoExons)
annoExons <- annoExons[!is.na(annoExons$gene_id), ]
nrow(annoExons)
```

Some parts of the data can be mapped to several gene names. As it is not easy to interpret results mapping to multiple genes, we will remove multiple mappings from the dataset. 

```{r}
annoExons <- as.data.table(annoExons)

# get min start and max stop position for one exon
annoExons <- annoExons[, list(chr = probesets.seqnames, start = min(probesets.start), end = max(probesets.end), gene_id = gene_id, gene_name = gene_name), by = exon_id]

# paste chr, start and stop together
annoExons <- annoExons[!duplicated(annoExons), ]
annoExons <- annoExons[ , new := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = ":")), .SDcols = -c(1, 4, 5, 6)]
annoExons <- annoExons[ , c(7, 1:6)]
annoExons <- annoExons[ , location := do.call(paste, c(.SD, sep = "-")), .SDcols = -c(2, 3, 4, 6, 7)]
annoExons <- annoExons[ , c(2, 8, 6, 7)]

# now remove exons with multiple gene id mappings
annoSummarized <- annoExons[, .(count = uniqueN(gene_id)), by = exon_id]  # group by exon and count number of different Ensemble gene ids
annoFiltered <- as.list(annoSummarized[annoSummarized$count > 1, "exon_id"])  # get exon ids with multiple Ensemble gene ids
idsToExclude <- (featureNames(exonSummaries) %in% annoFiltered$exon_id)
exonSummaries <- subset(exonSummaries, !idsToExclude)  # remove multi-mapped exons
fData(exonSummaries)$exon_id <- rownames(fData(exonSummaries))
fData(exonSummaries) <- left_join(fData(exonSummaries), annoExons)
rownames(fData(exonSummaries)) <- fData(exonSummaries)$exon_id
dim(exonSummaries)
```

Remove exons which are located on the X, Y or M chromosome as they are hard to interpret. 

```{r}
exonsToRemove <- annoExons[startsWith(annoExons$location, "chrX") | startsWith(annoExons$location, "chrY") | startsWith(annoExons$location, "chrM"), "exon_id"]
idsToExclude <- (featureNames(exonSummaries) %in% exonsToRemove$exon_id)
exonSummaries <- subset(exonSummaries, !idsToExclude)  # remove exons on chr X, Y and M
dim(exonSummaries)
```

Remove exons which have exactly the same expression values in all samples (so called multi-mapped samples). This is a necessary step, as we would count transcripts multiple times (mostly exons of the same gene) leading to high non-significant FDR (multiple testing) correction values in the differential expression analysis later. Instead of completely removing them, we just keep one of the duplicated rows and merge the gene, transcript, exon IDs together (separated by a vertical slash: |). We also do the same for all the annotation information in the feature data (fData) and save everything into a new ExonFeatureSet.

```{r}
# 1. Remove duplicated rows and merge rownames of duplicated rows together
expressions <- aggregate(rownames(exprs(exonSummaries)) ~., exprs(exonSummaries), paste, collapse = '|') 
rownames(expressions) <- expressions$`rownames(exprs(exonSummaries))`  # change rownames to new merged rownames
expressions$`rownames(exprs(exonSummaries))` <- NULL  # remove rownames column

# 2. Merge the annotation of the merged rownames as well
annoNew <- data.frame()
for (rows in rownames(expressions)) {
  if (grepl("\\|", rows)) {
    ids <- strsplit(rows, "\\|")
    idsAnno <- fData(exonSummaries)[rownames(fData(exonSummaries)) %in% ids[[1]], ]
    idsAnno <- t(data.frame(apply(idsAnno, 2, paste, collapse = "|")))
    rownames(idsAnno) <- rows
    annoNew <- rbind(annoNew, idsAnno)
  } else {
    annoNew <- rbind(annoNew, fData(exonSummaries)[rownames(fData(exonSummaries)) == rows, ])
  }
}

# 3. Generate new ExonFeatureSet
exonSummaries <- new("ExonFeatureSet", 
                     exprs = expressions, 
                     phenoData = phenoData(exonSummaries), 
                     featureData = AnnotatedDataFrame(annoNew) , 
                     experimentData = experimentData(exonSummaries), 
                     protocolData = protocolData(exonSummaries), 
                     annotation = "pd.huex.1.0.st.v2")
```

This reduced number of exons makes sense. Citation from the abstract of the publication from M. K. Sakharkar, V. T. Chow, and P. Kangueane (In Silico Biology, 2004): "The 26,564 annotated genes in the human genome (build October, 2003) contain 233,785 exons and 207,344 introns."

We do not have any NA's in the gene IDs and/or gene symbols, so we do not need to exclude them. Therefore, we can just save the annotated dataset into an RData file:

```{r}
save(exonSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/5_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_exon_summaries_annotated.RData")
rm(annoFiltered, annoSummarized, annoExons, exonsToRemove, idsToExclude)
```

## Batch correction

For the batch correction of the known batches (different generation times of the samples) of the microarrays, we will use ComBat from the Surrogate Variable Analysis (SVA) package. We have five batches (1: 64 samples, 2: 86 samples, 3,: 11 samples 4: 3 samples, A: 40 samples) included in the data. A plot as well as a more detailed description is given in the *02_QC_And_Plots.Rmd* script. 

```{r}
exprsRaw <- as.matrix(exprs(exonSummaries))
batch <- as.factor(pData(exonSummaries)$Batch)
modCombat <- model.matrix(~1, data = pData(exonSummaries))
exprsCombat <- ComBat(dat = exprsRaw, batch = batch, mod = modCombat, par.prior = TRUE, prior.plots = FALSE)
identical(rownames(exprs(exonSummaries)), rownames(exprsCombat)) # check if the two matrices are in the same order
exprs(exonSummaries) <- exprsCombat
dim(exonSummaries)
save(exonSummaries, file = "/storage/groups/ccm01/workspace/MPIP-Dean_postmortem_brain/04.DEX/RData_Files/6_affymetrix_exon_microarray_data_after_rma_probeset_summaries_filtered_exon_summaries_annotated_batch_corrected.RData")
rm(exonSummaries)
```
